question.text: Under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012, a Cat III AIF such as Aravalli Long-Short Fund can be constituted in ALL of the following legal forms EXCEPT one. Identify the incorrect option.

answer.text: Trust under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882
Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008
Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) under the Hindu Law
Company under the Companies Act, 2013 or a body corporate set up under an Act of Parliament

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012 permit an AIF to be set up as a trust, an LLP, a company, or a body corporate under an Act of Parliament/State Legislature. HUF is NOT a permitted legal form. A HUF cannot hold an AIF; it may only be an investor in an AIF. **The Trap:** HUFs are commonly-used vehicles for family wealth and can INVEST in an AIF, so it sounds plausible. But for the AIF itself, only trust/LLP/company/statutory body corporate are valid constitutional forms. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C / XIX-D / XIX-A all share this list. XIX-B distributors must know the same list when explaining fund constitution to HNI clients. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For a Cat III hedge-fund desk, the trust form is near-universal — operational flexibility, investor confidentiality and tax treatment outweigh LLP/company choices in almost every commercial case.
